name: Mac Michaels

tenures.source: the fed's own dated show results (read for this accession, not served) and its own Title History page (promotions/newa-mid-atlantic/archive/title-history.html)
tenures.note: Held the NeWA Mid-Atlantic Heavyweight Championship twice. Already reigning champion by 17 January 1999, when Lycos pinned him with a foreign object (a "slap jack") to take the title; lost a separate non-title match to The Wraith by disqualification the night before, 16 January 1999. Won the title back in a Four Corners Match, 10 February 1999 — the only reign the fed's own Title History page attests; no document says whether this second win came against Lycos directly or a title left vacant.

caption: Lost the Mid-Atlantic Heavyweight Championship to Lycos, then won it back three weeks later in a Four Corners Match — the only reign the fed's own Title History page records.

name: JD Johnson

tenures.source: the fed's own dated show results (read for this accession, not served) and its own News page (promotions/newa-mid-atlantic/archive/news.html)
tenures.note: Won the Mid-Atlantic Television Title from its reigning champion, Fred Rogers, in a two-out-of-three-falls match, 15 January 1999, then lost it to KRaZ-e the very next night. The fed's own News page (27 January 1999) later calls him and KRaZ-e "two former champions" of an unqualified "Mid-Atlantic Title" and orders the pair into a best-of-seven series for the Television Title — a decree dated ten to twelve days after both men's own January matches, so it did not cause them; no result for the ordered series survives anywhere held. Also lost a non-title match to Mark Mass, 22 January 1999.

caption: Won the Mid-Atlantic Television Title from its reigning champion, then lost it the very next night.

name: KRaZ-e

tenures.source: the fed's own dated show results (read for this accession, not served) and its own News page (promotions/newa-mid-atlantic/archive/news.html)
tenures.note: Won the Mid-Atlantic Television Title from JD Johnson, 16 January 1999, and retained it against John Cole the following night. Stripped of the title by Jim Crockett, Jr. on 27 January 1999, citing his and JD Johnson's own prior conduct, and ordered into a best-of-seven series against Johnson to decide it (promotions/newa-mid-atlantic/archive/news.html) — no result for that series survives; Fred Rogers is next attested champion by 10 February 1999, via a Three Way Elimination Match the fed's own Title History page names without saying who else stood in it.
Lost to Mr. Kool by submission in a non-title match at Gaslaw Gala.

caption: Won the Mid-Atlantic Television Title from JD Johnson and retained it once, before being stripped of it for misconduct three weeks later.

name: Fred Rogers

tenures.source: the fed's own dated show results (read for this accession, not served) and its own Title History page (promotions/newa-mid-atlantic/archive/title-history.html)
tenures.note: Held the Mid-Atlantic Television Title before 15 January 1999 — an earlier reign attested only by its own end, dated no further than "before 15 January 1999" — and lost it to JD Johnson that night in a two-out-of-three-falls match; lost a separate non-title match the next night, 16 January 1999, to X-Poison's own B. Cobra. Won the Television Title a second time in a Three Way Elimination Match, 10 February 1999 — the only reign the fed's own Title History page attests for him.

caption: Lost the Mid-Atlantic Television Title to JD Johnson, then won it back three and a half weeks later in a Three Way Elimination Match.

name: Lycos

tenures.source: the fed's own dated show results (read for this accession, not served) and its own News page (promotions/newa-mid-atlantic/archive/news.html)
tenures.note: Won the NeWA Mid-Atlantic Heavyweight Title from Mac Michaels by pinfall, with a foreign object (a "slap jack"), 17 January 1999. Billed as reigning "Mid-Atlantic Champion" ten days later in the fed's own News page (27 January 1999), submitted for a unification match against "EWC" Television Champion HICAL at the NeWA PPV Lord of the Rings, the winner promised a shot at the NeWA World or International Champion. No document records how or when this reign ended; the fed's own Title History page omits Lycos and this entire reign, next attesting Mac Michaels champion again by 10 February 1999.

caption: Won the Mid-Atlantic Heavyweight Title from Mac Michaels with a foreign object, then was billed as reigning champion ten days later — the record goes quiet on how the reign ended.

name: HICAL

tenures.source: the fed's own dated show results (read for this accession, not served) and its own News page (promotions/newa-mid-atlantic/archive/news.html)
tenures.note: Named twice on the fed's own dated show results: lost a fall to Dan (of X-Poison) in a Number-One-Contenders Triangle Match, 17 January 1999, and lost a No-Time-Limit Falls-Count-Anywhere Match to The Wraith, 22 January 1999. Billed as "EWC T.V Champion" opposite Mid-Atlantic Champion Lycos for a unification match at the NeWA PPV Lord of the Rings, per the fed's own News page (27 January 1999) — no promotion called "EWC," and no Mid-Atlantic title of his own, is otherwise attested anywhere in this wing's own held corpus.

Eliminated last in the Four Man Battle Royale for the BCW National Title, 4 April 1999, after briefly claiming a last-man-standing win the match continued past. The fed's own Title History page traces two further National Championship reigns for HICAL (beating The Wraith; beating Titan a second time, read [sic] as "HICAL 2 Titan"). Billed as touring in Canada for a NeWA World T.V. Title match at Gaslaw Gala but ran in during the main event instead, attacking both Rowdy Piper and Titan before Rowdy Piper's own finish.

entrance_music.corrected: "Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap" by AC/DC

tenures.style: Technician, Brawler, Wrestler, Old Style, Shooter

caption: A visiting wrestler on the Mid-Atlantic's own undercard, twice beaten, then billed under an outside "EWC" banner as its Television Champion for a cross-promotion unification match.

identity.note: HICAL is a generic ring name already independently reused across held promotions (see euwc-hical's own identity note, itself distinct-presumed against hical-lcw-1997 and hical-wccw). No document ties this wing's own HICAL, billed from an unidentified "EWC," to EUWC's own HICAL (a three-time EUWC World Heavyweight Champion, 1997-1999, never billed with a Television title), to LCW-1997's own HICAL (first attested by 2000-05, after this wing's own window closes), or to wccw's own HICAL (a single Round 1 loss in an August 1999 NeWA-hub-wide tournament, seven months after this wing's own held window) — a third instance of the same name on a third NeWA-hub member territory is suggestive, given the hub's own attested cross-territory roster movement (see this wing's own Affiliations for the Angels of the Night precedent), but no document names any two of the three HICALs together; presumed distinct per the collision rule's no-auto-merge discipline, the shared name recorded, not resolved.
No shared roster, era, or hub connection to EUWC — coincidental collision, not evidence of a link.

name: Ryan Carling

tenures.source: the fed's own dated show results (read for this accession, not served) and its own Title History page (promotions/newa-mid-atlantic/archive/title-history.html)
tenures.note: Won the vacant Mid-Atlantic Light-Heavyweight Title in a No-Time-Limit Triangle Match over David Corning and Sean Storm, 15 January 1999, and retained it in a Four Corners Match against Sean Storm, Johnny Citizen and Brent Morris, 17 January 1999. The fed's own Title History page names no "Light-Heavyweight" title at all, only an empty "Light-Weight" row — almost certainly the same belt under a variant name.

caption: Won the vacant Mid-Atlantic Light-Heavyweight Title and retained it once; the fed's own Title History page names the belt only as a variant, "Light-Weight," with no entries of its own.
